rows.scope: Apply mathematical knowledge to everyday, societal and workplace problems.
Analyze givens, plan and solve, justify conclusions, then judge whether the solution and method are reasonable.
Choose suitable physical tools, manipulatives, paper-and-pencil and technology alongside estimation and mental arithmetic.
Explain mathematical reasoning with symbols, diagrams, graphs and words.
Build and use representations for organizing, recording and communicating mathematical ideas.
Analyze mathematical relationships and explain connections between ideas.
State and justify mathematical arguments with precise written and spoken language.
Determine domain and range of linear functions; choose realistic discrete or continuous values and express restrictions using inequalities.
Write two-variable line equations in slope-intercept, standard and point-slope form given slope/point or two points.
Model two-variable linear equations from tables, graphs and verbal descriptions.
Write and solve direct-variation equations.
Find a line equation through a point parallel to a specified line.
Find a line equation through a point perpendicular to a specified line.
Write horizontal or vertical line equations and distinguish zero from undefined slope.
Write inequalities in two variables from a table, graph or verbal model.
Write a two-equation, two-variable linear system from tabular, graphical or verbal data.
Use similar right triangles to justify invariant slope between any two points on a line using rise over run.
Graph proportional relationships and interpret their unit rate as line slope.
Determine slope from tables, graphs, two points and line equations, including slope-intercept, standard and point-slope forms.
Find linear rate of change from tables, graphs or equations in mathematical and real-world contexts.
Find line slope/rate of change and y-intercept from table or graph in applied and mathematical settings.
Graph linear functions and identify x/y-intercepts, zeros and slopes in mathematical and applied settings.
Represent the solution region of a two-variable linear inequality on a coordinate plane.
Investigate the graph of f(x)=x under af(x), f(x)+d, f(x-c), f(bx) for given constants.
Graph two-equation linear systems in two variables and find solutions when they exist.
Estimate solutions graphically for two-variable two-equation linear systems arising from real situations.
Graph the simultaneous solution set of a system of two-variable linear inequalities.
Create a scatterplot and classify two-variable associations as linear, nonlinear or none.
Contrast plotted bivariate data with and without a suggestive linear relationship.
Use an approximate linear trend line to predict from bivariate data.
Calculate a correlation coefficient with technology and interpret its strength-of-linear-association meaning.
Distinguish real-world association from a cause-and-effect conclusion.
Fit an approximate linear function to data, with and without technology, to estimate and predict in real contexts.
Solve one-variable linear equations, including distribution and variables on both sides.
Solve one-variable linear inequalities, including distribution and variables on both sides.
Solve two-equation linear systems in two variables in mathematical and real-world contexts.
Determine quadratic-function domain and range, reporting restrictions through inequalities.
Build quadratic equations from a vertex and another point in vertex form and convert to standard form.
Construct quadratics given real roots and a related graph.
Graph quadratics and identify possible intercepts, zeros, maximum/minimum, vertex and axis of symmetry.
Relate factors of quadratic expressions to zeros of their associated functions.
Investigate graphs of parent f(x)=x² under af(x), f(x)+d, f(x-c), f(bx) for specified constants.
Solve quadratic equations having real roots by factoring, square-root extraction, completing the square and quadratic formula.
Use technology to fit quadratics to data and use them for real-world prediction/estimation.
Determine domain and range of f(x)=ab^x and express restrictions as inequalities.
Interpret coefficients a and b in real-context models f(x)=ab^x.
Model growth and decay as f(x)=ab^x, using rational base b, in mathematical and real-world situations.
Graph exponential growth/decay and identify y-intercept and asymptote in applied problems.
Use technology to fit an exponential model to data and make real-world predictions.
Add and subtract first- and second-degree polynomials.
Multiply first- and second-degree polynomials.
Divide polynomials of degree one or two by polynomial divisors of degree one or two, only when divisor degree is no larger than dividend degree.
Use distribution to rewrite first- and second-degree polynomials into equivalent forms.
Factor quadratic trinomials ax²+bx+c over real factors when possible, including perfect-square trinomials.
Recognize differences of two squares and rewrite such binomials via their algebraic structure.
Simplify numeric radical expressions involving square roots.
Simplify numeric and symbolic expressions using integer and rational exponent laws.

editorial_rule: Preserve parent stems/subpart letters and material qualifiers. No implied equivalence with traditional §111.39 Algebra I.
